claim: CCR4 is predominantly expressed on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs under normocholesterolemic or hypercholesterolemic conditions.
source: Notably, CCR4 expression was expressed on approximately 15–25% of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs from wild-type or Apoe-/- mice (Appendix 1—figure 1A–C), while CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs from these mice expressed CCR4 at markedly lower levels, suggesting that CCR4 is predominantly expressed on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and that hypercholesterolemia does not affect CCR4 expression.
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis data from peripheral LNs, spleen, and para-aortic LNs showing CCR4 expression levels on different T cell populations, with reference to Appendix 1—figure 1A–C.

claim: Hypercholesterolemia does not affect CCR4 expression on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs.
source: Notably, CCR4 expression was expressed on approximately 15–25% of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs from wild-type or Apoe-/- mice (Appendix 1—figure 1A–C), while CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs from these mice expressed CCR4 at markedly lower levels, suggesting that CCR4 is predominantly expressed on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and that hypercholesterolemia does not affect CCR4 expression.
evidence: Comparison of CCR4 expression between wild-type and Apoe-/- mice showing similar expression levels.

claim: CCR4 expression in CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in the atherosclerotic aorta is much higher than in CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs.
source: We also examined CCR4 expression on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in the atherosclerotic aorta of Apoe-/- mice and consistently found that CCR4 expression in CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs was much higher than that in CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs (Appendix 1—figure 1D).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of CCR4 expression in aortic T cells, with reference to Appendix 1—figure 1D.

claim: CCL17 and CCL22 are highly expressed by dendritic cells in lymph nodes.
source: As CCL17 and CCL22, known as specific ligands for CCR4, are highly expressed by dendritic cells (DCs) in LNs (Alferink et al., 2003; Tang and Cyster, 1999), we examined their expression in the peripheral LNs of wild-type, Apoe-/-, and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice by immunohistochemistry.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Alferink et al., 2003; Tang and Cyster, 1999).

claim: CCL17 and CCL22 are expressed in the peripheral lymph nodes of wild-type, Apoe-/-, and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: As expected, clear expression of these chemokines was observed in the peripheral LNs of wild-type, Apoe-/-, and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Appendix 2—figure 1).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing chemokine expression in peripheral LNs, with reference to Appendix 2—figure 1.

claim: CCL17 is expressed in atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: CCL17 expression was detected in the atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, and some lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages expressed this chemokine (Appendix 3—figure 1A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing CCL17 expression in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Appendix 3—figure 1A.

claim: CCL17 is not detected in the aorta of wild-type mice without atherosclerotic plaques.
source: However, CCL17 expression was not detected in the aorta of wild-type mice without atherosclerotic plaques (Appendix 3—figure 1A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing absence of CCL17 in wild-type mouse aorta, with reference to Appendix 3—figure 1A.

claim: Some lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages express CCL17 in atherosclerotic lesions.
source: CCL17 expression was detected in the atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, and some lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages expressed this chemokine (Appendix 3—figure 1A).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing colocalization of CCL17 with MOMA-2+ macrophages, with reference to Appendix 3—figure 1A.

claim: CCL22 is modestly expressed in atherosclerotic lesions and partially colocalizes with lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages in Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Another ligand CCL22 was modestly expressed in atherosclerotic lesions and partially colocalized with lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages in Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, while its expression was not detected in the aorta of wild-type mice (Appendix 3—figure 1B).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing CCL22 expression and colocalization with macrophages, with reference to Appendix 3—figure 1B.

claim: CCL22 expression is not detected in the aorta of wild-type mice.
source: Another ligand CCL22 was modestly expressed in atherosclerotic lesions and partially colocalized with lesional MOMA-2+ macrophages in Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, while its expression was not detected in the aorta of wild-type mice (Appendix 3—figure 1B).
evidence: Immunohistochemistry data showing absence of CCL22 in wild-type mouse aorta, with reference to Appendix 3—figure 1B.

claim: Tregs may migrate to peripheral lymph nodes and atherosclerotic lesions partly via the CCL17/CCL22–CCR4 axes under hypercholesterolemia.
source: Together, these findings suggest that Tregs may migrate to peripheral LNs and atherosclerotic lesions partly via the CCL17/CCL22–CCR4 axes under hypercholesterolemia.
evidence: Inference based on the expression patterns of CCR4 on Tregs and CCL17/CCL22 in lymphoid tissues and atherosclerotic lesions.

claim: Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice developed normally without any spontaneous inflammatory disease.
source: Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice developed normally without any spontaneous inflammatory disease.
evidence: Observational statement about the phenotype of the knockout mice.

claim: Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice exhibit a significant increase in atherosclerotic lesion size in the aortic sinus compared with Apoe-/- mice.
source: Notably, compared with Apoe-/- mice, Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice exhibited a significant increase in atherosclerotic lesion size in the aortic sinus (aortic sinus mean plaque area: control Apoe-/- mice: 1.46±0.50×105 μm2 versus Ccr4-/-Apoe-/-: 2.04±0.82 × 105 μm2, p<0.05; Figure 1A).
evidence: Quantitative analysis of atherosclerotic lesion area in aortic sinus with statistical comparison, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: There is no significant difference in aortic plaque burden in thoracoabdominal aortas between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: In parallel with the cross-sectional studies, we performed en face analysis of thoracoabdominal aortas, revealing no significant difference in aortic plaque burden between the two groups (Figure 1B).
evidence: En face analysis data showing no difference in plaque burden, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: There are no significant differences in body weight or plasma lipid profile between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice at 18 weeks of age.
source: There were no significant differences in body weight or plasma lipid profile between the two groups (Table 1).
evidence: Biochemical measurements showing no differences in body weight or lipid parameters, with reference to Table 1.

claim: Atherosclerotic lesions of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice show a 20% increase in macrophage accumulation compared to Apoe-/- mice.
source: Notably, compared with those of Apoe-/- mice, the atherosclerotic lesions of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice showed a 20% increase in macrophage accumulation (Figure 1C) and a marked 42% increase in CD4+ T cell infiltration (Figure 1D).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of macrophages in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Atherosclerotic lesions of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice show a marked 42% increase in CD4+ T cell infiltration compared to Apoe-/- mice.
source: Notably, compared with those of Apoe-/- mice, the atherosclerotic lesions of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice showed a 20% increase in macrophage accumulation (Figure 1C) and a marked 42% increase in CD4+ T cell infiltration (Figure 1D).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of CD4+ T cells in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Few Foxp3+ Tregs are found within the plaques of Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: In addition, we performed immunohistochemical analysis of Foxp3+ Tregs in atherosclerotic lesions using an anti-Foxp3 antibody. However, few Foxp3+ Tregs were found within the plaques of Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (data not shown).
evidence: Immunohistochemical analysis showing minimal Foxp3+ Tregs in plaques.

claim: The proportion of collagen in the aortic sinus plaques of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice is significantly lower than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: The proportion of collagen in the aortic sinus plaques of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice was significantly lower than that in the aortic sinus plaques of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Histological quantification of collagen content in atherosclerotic plaques, with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: CCR4 plays a role in preventing the development of early atherosclerotic lesions and inducing a less inflammatory plaque phenotype.
source: These findings on atherosclerotic plaque size and components collectively suggest that CCR4 plays a role in preventing the development of early atherosclerotic lesions and inducing a less inflammatory plaque phenotype.
evidence: Inference based on the combined data on plaque size, macrophage accumulation, T cell infiltration, and collagen content.

claim: The mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (Il1b and Il6) is markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: The mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (Il1b and Il6), Th1-related Tbx21, and Th17-related Rorc was markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, indicating augmented proatherogenic immune responses in the atherosclerotic aorta (Figure 1F).
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of cytokine mRNA expression in aorta, with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: The mRNA expression of Th1-related Tbx21 is markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: The mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (Il1b and Il6), Th1-related Tbx21, and Th17-related Rorc was markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, indicating augmented proatherogenic immune responses in the atherosclerotic aorta (Figure 1F).
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of Tbx21 mRNA expression in aorta, with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: The mRNA expression of Th17-related Rorc is markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: The mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (Il1b and Il6), Th1-related Tbx21, and Th17-related Rorc was markedly upregulated in the aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, indicating augmented proatherogenic immune responses in the atherosclerotic aorta (Figure 1F).
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of Rorc mRNA expression in aorta, with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: The mRNA expression of the Treg-specific transcription factor Foxp3 is undetectable in the aorta.
source: The mRNA expression of the Treg-specific transcription factor Foxp3 was undetectable.
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis showing Foxp3 mRNA below detection limits.

claim: CCR4 deficiency promotes the accumulation of inflammatory cells and proinflammatory immune responses in the aorta, leading to augmented development of early atherosclerotic lesions in the aortic root.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that CCR4 deficiency promotes the accumulation of inflammatory cells and proinflammatory immune responses in the aorta, leading to augmented development of early atherosclerotic lesions in the aortic root.
evidence: Summary inference based on multiple lines of data including plaque size, inflammatory cell accumulation, and cytokine expression.

claim: The frequencies of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs are significantly higher in the spleen of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in age-matched Apoe-/- mice.
source: The frequencies of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells were significantly higher in the spleen of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of age-matched Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of Treg frequencies in spleen, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The frequencies of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells are significantly higher in the spleen of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in age-matched Apoe-/- mice.
source: The frequencies of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells were significantly higher in the spleen of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of age-matched Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of effector memory T cell frequencies in spleen, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The absolute numbers of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs are significantly higher in the peripheral lymph nodes of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in age-matched Apoe-/- mice.
source: The absolute numbers of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells were significantly higher in the peripheral LNs of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than those of age-matched Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of absolute Treg numbers in peripheral LNs, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The absolute numbers of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells are significantly higher in the peripheral lymph nodes of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in age-matched Apoe-/- mice.
source: The absolute numbers of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells were significantly higher in the peripheral LNs of 8- or 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than those of age-matched Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of absolute effector memory T cell numbers in peripheral LNs, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The absolute number of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells is higher in the spleen of 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in age-matched Apoe-/- mice.
source: The absolute number of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells was also higher in the spleen of 18-week-old Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than that of age-matched Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of absolute effector memory T cell numbers in spleen, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Similar results for Treg and effector memory T cell expansion were obtained for normocholesterolemic wild-type mice.
source: Similar results were obtained for normocholesterolemic wild-type mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B), suggesting that the expansion of Tregs and effector memory T cells in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice is independent of hypercholesterolemia.
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis in wild-type mice showing similar patterns, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The expansion of Tregs and effector memory T cells in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice is independent of hypercholesterolemia.
source: Similar results were obtained for normocholesterolemic wild-type mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B), suggesting that the expansion of Tregs and effector memory T cells in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice is independent of hypercholesterolemia.
evidence: Comparison of results between hypercholesterolemic and normocholesterolemic mice showing similar patterns.

claim: The proportions of Ki-67-positive Tregs are markedly higher in the peripheral lymph nodes and spleen of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: We evaluated the proliferative capacity of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs by analyzing Ki-67 expression using flow cytometry and found that the proportions of Ki-67-positive Tregs and non-Tregs were markedly higher in the peripheral LNs and spleen of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of Ki-67 expression in Tregs, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The proportions of Ki-67-positive non-Tregs are markedly higher in the peripheral lymph nodes and spleen of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: We evaluated the proliferative capacity of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs by analyzing Ki-67 expression using flow cytometry and found that the proportions of Ki-67-positive Tregs and non-Tregs were markedly higher in the peripheral LNs and spleen of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of Ki-67 expression in non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: There is no difference in the development of thymic T cells between 4-week-old Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: To determine the effect of CCR4 deficiency on T cell development in the thymus, we performed flow cytometric analysis of thymocytes from 4-week-old Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice and found no difference in the development of thymic T cells between the two groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of thymocyte populations, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: There is no difference in the frequency of thymic CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs between 4-week-old Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: In line with a previous report in normocholesterolemic mice (Lee et al., 2005), there was no difference in the frequency of thymic CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs between the two groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of thymic Tregs, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and citation to Lee et al., 2005.

claim: The increased numbers of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs in peripheral lymph nodes are due to their enhanced proliferative capacity but not to their promoted development in the thymus.
source: These data indicate that the increased numbers of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs and CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs in peripheral LNs are due to their enhanced proliferative capacity but not to their promoted development in the thymus.
evidence: Inference based on Ki-67 proliferation data and thymic development data.

claim: CD86 expression on dendritic cells is upregulated in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: We also analyzed other immune cells in the spleen of Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice by flow cytometry and found no major differences in the proportions or activation-associated molecule expression between the two groups, except for CD86 expression on DCs which was upregulated in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of DC activation markers, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: CCR4 deficiency has no major effect on the expression of CTLA-4 or CD103 in CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in peripheral lymph nodes.
source: Notably, CCR4 deficiency had no major effect on the expression of cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) or CD103 in CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs (Figure 2E).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of activation markers on Tregs, with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: There are no significant differences in the mRNA expression of activation- or function-associated molecules in splenic Tregs between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: In line with the data on peripheral LNs, there were no significant differences in the mRNA expression of these molecules between the two groups (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of Treg-associated molecules, with reference to Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The expression of the activation marker CTLA-4 in peripheral lymph node CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs is higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: In contrast to the results on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs, the expression of the activation marker CTLA-4 in peripheral LN CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs was higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, although the expression of another activation marker CD103 was not altered by CCR4 deficiency (Figure 2G).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of activation markers on non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: The expression of CD103 in peripheral lymph node CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs is not altered by CCR4 deficiency.
source: In contrast to the results on CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs, the expression of the activation marker CTLA-4 in peripheral LN CD4+Foxp3- non-Tregs was higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, although the expression of another activation marker CD103 was not altered by CCR4 deficiency (Figure 2G).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of activation markers on non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: There is a marked increase in the mRNA expression of activation-associated molecules (Ctla4, Cd44, and Cd103) in splenic non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: We found a marked increase in the mRNA expression of activation-associated molecules (Ctla4, Cd44, and Cd103) in splenic non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2H).
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of activation markers in non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 2H.

claim: Upregulated mRNA expression of various chemokine receptors, including Th1-related Ccr1, Cxcr3, and Cx3cr1, Th2-related Ccr8, and Th17-related Ccr6, is observed in splenic non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: We also observed upregulated mRNA expression of various chemokine receptors, including Th1-related Ccr1, Cxcr3, and Cx3cr1, Th2-related Ccr8, and Th17-related Ccr6 in splenic non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B), indicating that CCR4 deficiency may promote the activation and expansion of helper T cells and facilitate their migration to atherosclerotic lesions.
evidence: Quantitative reverse transcription PCR analysis of chemokine receptors in non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: CCR4 deficiency may promote the activation and expansion of helper T cells and facilitate their migration to atherosclerotic lesions.
source: We also observed upregulated mRNA expression of various chemokine receptors, including Th1-related Ccr1, Cxcr3, and Cx3cr1, Th2-related Ccr8, and Th17-related Ccr6 in splenic non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B), indicating that CCR4 deficiency may promote the activation and expansion of helper T cells and facilitate their migration to atherosclerotic lesions.
evidence: Inference based on upregulated chemokine receptor expression in non-Tregs.

claim: Augmented Teff immune responses may affect atherosclerosis more strongly than the increase in Tregs in peripheral lymphoid tissues.
source: Considering the accelerated early atherosclerosis observed in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, these results indicate that augmented Teff immune responses may affect atherosclerosis more strongly than the increase in Tregs in peripheral lymphoid tissues.
evidence: Inference based on the net effect of increased Tregs and increased Teff responses on atherosclerosis.

claim: The fraction of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells in the peripheral lymph nodes is significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: The fraction of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells in the peripheral LNs was significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, while there were no differences in the fractions of other CD4+ T cell subsets including interleukin (IL)-4-producing Th2 cells, IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells between the two groups (Figure 3A).
evidence: Intracellular cytokine staining and flow cytometric analysis of Th1 cells in peripheral LNs, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: There are no differences in the fractions of IL-4-producing Th2 cells, IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells in peripheral lymph nodes between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: The fraction of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells in the peripheral LNs was significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, while there were no differences in the fractions of other CD4+ T cell subsets including interleukin (IL)-4-producing Th2 cells, IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells between the two groups (Figure 3A).
evidence: Intracellular cytokine staining and flow cytometric analysis of various T cell subsets in peripheral LNs, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The fraction of splenic Th1 cells is higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: In line with this, the fraction of splenic Th1 cells was higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, although the proportion of IL-17-producing Th17 cells was also higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: Intracellular cytokine staining and flow cytometric analysis of Th1 cells in spleen, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The proportion of IL-17-producing Th17 cells in the spleen is higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: In line with this, the fraction of splenic Th1 cells was higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, although the proportion of IL-17-producing Th17 cells was also higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: Intracellular cytokine staining and flow cytometric analysis of Th17 cells in spleen, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Splenic CD4+ T cells from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice secrete more Th1-related cytokine IFN-γ, Th2-related cytokine IL-13, Th17-related cytokine IL-17, and various inflammation-related cytokines and chemokines compared to those from Apoe-/- mice.
source: Compared with those from Apoe-/- mice, splenic CD4+ T cells from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice secreted more Th1-related cytokine IFN-γ, Th2-related cytokine IL-13, Th17-related cytokine IL-17, and various inflammation-related cytokines and chemokines (Figure 3C).
evidence: Cytokine array analysis of culture supernatants from stimulated CD4+ T cells, with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: ELISA analysis confirms that the IFN-γ and IL-17 levels in the cell supernatants of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice are much higher than those in Apoe-/- mice.
source: ELISA analysis confirmed that the IFN-γ and IL-17 levels in the cell supernatants of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice were much higher than those in the cell supernatants of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: ELISA measurements of cytokine concentrations in culture supernatants, with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: ELISA analysis reveals higher IL-4 and IL-10 production in splenic CD4+ T cells from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those from Apoe-/- mice.
source: Although the cytokine levels of Th2-related cytokine IL-4 and Treg-related anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 were below the detectable levels by cytokine array analysis, ELISA analysis revealed higher IL-4 and IL-10 production in splenic CD4+ T cells from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those from Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3D), which may be compensatory immune responses to the proinflammatory T cell responses caused by CCR4 deficiency.
evidence: ELISA measurements of IL-4 and IL-10 concentrations in culture supernatants, with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: Higher IL-4 and IL-10 production in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice may be compensatory immune responses to the proinflammatory T cell responses caused by CCR4 deficiency.
source: Although the cytokine levels of Th2-related cytokine IL-4 and Treg-related anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 were below the detectable levels by cytokine array analysis, ELISA analysis revealed higher IL-4 and IL-10 production in splenic CD4+ T cells from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those from Apoe-/- mice (Figure 3D), which may be compensatory immune responses to the proinflammatory T cell responses caused by CCR4 deficiency.
evidence: Inference based on the pattern of cytokine production in the context of CCR4 deficiency.

claim: The frequency and number of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs are significantly higher in the para-aortic lymph nodes of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice.
source: Consistent with the peripheral LN data, the frequency and number of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs were significantly higher in the para-aortic LNs of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of Tregs in para-aortic LNs, with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: The number of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells is significantly higher in the para-aortic lymph nodes of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice.
source: The number of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells was significantly higher in the para-aortic LNs of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice, while their frequency did not differ between the two groups (Figure 4B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of effector memory T cells in para-aortic LNs, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The frequency of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells in para-aortic lymph nodes does not differ between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: The number of CD4+CD44highCD62Llow effector memory T cells was significantly higher in the para-aortic LNs of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in those of Apoe-/- mice, while their frequency did not differ between the two groups (Figure 4B).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of effector memory T cells in para-aortic LNs, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: There are no significant differences in the expression of activation- or function-associated molecules or chemokine receptors in para-aortic lymph node Tregs between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: In line with the data on peripheral lymphoid tissues, there were no significant differences in the expression of activation- or function-associated molecules or chemokine receptors in para-aortic LN Tregs between the two groups (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2A).
evidence: Flow cytometric and qPCR analysis of Treg markers in para-aortic LNs, with reference to Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2A.

claim: The expression of Cd103 is upregulated in para-aortic lymph node non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Notably, the expression of Cd103 and Th1-related Tbx21 was upregulated in para-aortic LN non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, while the expression of other activation- or helper T cell-associated molecules or chemokine receptors was unaltered (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: qPCR analysis of gene expression in para-aortic LN non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: The expression of Th1-related Tbx21 is upregulated in para-aortic lymph node non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Notably, the expression of Cd103 and Th1-related Tbx21 was upregulated in para-aortic LN non-Tregs from Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice, while the expression of other activation- or helper T cell-associated molecules or chemokine receptors was unaltered (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: qPCR analysis of gene expression in para-aortic LN non-Tregs, with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: The fractions of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells, IL-4-producing Th2 cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells in para-aortic lymph nodes are significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of helper T cell subsets in para-aortic LNs revealed that the fractions of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells, IL-4-producing Th2 cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells were significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, suggesting augmented proinflammatory CD4+ T cell immune responses by CCR4 deficiency (Figure 4E).
evidence: Intracellular cytokine staining and flow cytometric analysis of T cell subsets in para-aortic LNs, with reference to Figure 4E.

claim: CCR4 deficiency augments proinflammatory CD4+ T cell immune responses in para-aortic lymph nodes.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of helper T cell subsets in para-aortic LNs revealed that the fractions of IFN-γ-producing Th1 cells, IL-4-producing Th2 cells, and IL-17-producing Th17 cells were significantly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, suggesting augmented proinflammatory CD4+ T cell immune responses by CCR4 deficiency (Figure 4E).
evidence: Inference based on increased frequencies of multiple proinflammatory T cell subsets.

claim: The frequency of aortic T-bet-expressing Th1 cells is markedly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice.
source: Strikingly, the frequency of aortic T-bet-expressing Th1 cells was markedly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, while the proportions of Th2 and Th17 subsets did not differ between the two groups (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of T-bet+ Th1 cells in atherosclerotic aorta, with reference to Figure 4F.

claim: The proportions of aortic Th2 and Th17 subsets do not differ between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Strikingly, the frequency of aortic T-bet-expressing Th1 cells was markedly higher in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice than in Apoe-/- mice, while the proportions of Th2 and Th17 subsets did not differ between the two groups (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of GATA3+ Th2 and RORγt+ Th17 cells in atherosclerotic aorta, with reference to Figure 4G–H.

claim: There is no difference in the proportion of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in the atherosclerotic aorta between Apoe-/- and Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: We next analyzed the accumulation of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in the atherosclerotic aorta by flow cytometry and found no difference in the proportion of CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs between the two groups (Figure 4I).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of Foxp3+ Tregs in atherosclerotic aorta, with reference to Figure 4I.

claim: There is a marked increase in the ratio of T-bet-expressing Th1 cells to CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs in the atherosclerotic aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Importantly, we found a marked increase in the ratio of T-bet-expressing Th1 cells to CD4+Foxp3+ Tregs (Th1 cell/Treg ratio) in the atherosclerotic aorta of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 4J), indicating Th1-skewed immune responses in the atherosclerotic lesions of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis calculating the Th1 cell/Treg ratio in atherosclerotic aorta, with reference to Figure 4J.

claim: CCR4 deficiency promotes the selective accumulation of proatherogenic Th1 cells in atherosclerotic aorta and shifts the Th1 cell/Treg balance toward Th1 cell responses.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that CCR4 deficiency promotes the selective accumulation of proatherogenic Th1 cells in atherosclerotic aorta and the accumulation of various helper T cell subsets including Th1 cells in para-aortic LNs and shifts the Th1 cell/Treg balance toward Th1 cell responses in atherosclerotic aorta, leading to exacerbated aortic inflammation and early atherosclerosis.
evidence: Summary inference based on multiple lines of data on T cell subsets in para-aortic LNs and atherosclerotic aorta.

claim: CCR4 deficiency significantly impairs the suppressive function of Tregs isolated from hypercholesterolemic mice.
source: Interestingly, CCR4 deficiency significantly impaired the suppressive function of Tregs isolated from hypercholesterolemic mice (Figure 5A), indicating that CCR4 expression on Tregs may be important for the regulation of proinflammatory immune responses and the development of early atherosclerosis.
evidence: In vitro suppression assay measuring Treg suppressive function, with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: CCR4 expression on Tregs may be important for the regulation of proinflammatory immune responses and the development of early atherosclerosis.
source: Interestingly, CCR4 deficiency significantly impaired the suppressive function of Tregs isolated from hypercholesterolemic mice (Figure 5A), indicating that CCR4 expression on Tregs may be important for the regulation of proinflammatory immune responses and the development of early atherosclerosis.
evidence: Inference based on the impaired suppressive function of CCR4-deficient Tregs.

claim: The upregulation of CD80 and CD86 expression on dendritic cells mediated by conventional T cells is markedly suppressed by coculture with Tregs from Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: As expected, the upregulation of CD80 and CD86 expression on DCs mediated by conventional T cells was markedly suppressed by coculture with Tregs from Apoe-/- or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice (Figure 5C).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of DC activation markers in coculture experiments, with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: The suppressive effect of CCR4-deficient Tregs on dendritic cell activation is significantly attenuated compared with that of CCR4-intact Tregs.
source: Notably, the suppressive effect of CCR4-deficient Tregs was significantly attenuated compared with that of CCR4-intact Tregs (Figure 5C).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis comparing the suppressive effects of CCR4-intact and CCR4-deficient Tregs on DC activation, with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: IFN-γ production by conventional T cells is markedly suppressed by coculture with CCR4-intact Tregs.
source: IFN-γ production by conventional T cells was markedly suppressed by coculture with CCR4-intact Tregs, while it was not significantly affected by coculture with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 5D).
evidence: ELISA measurements of IFN-γ in coculture experiments, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: IFN-γ production by conventional T cells is not significantly affected by coculture with CCR4-deficient Tregs.
source: IFN-γ production by conventional T cells was markedly suppressed by coculture with CCR4-intact Tregs, while it was not significantly affected by coculture with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 5D).
evidence: ELISA measurements of IFN-γ in coculture experiments, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: There is a marked difference in the ability to suppress the production of IFN-γ from conventional T cells between CCR4-intact Tregs and CCR4-deficient Tregs.
source: Importantly, there was a marked difference in the ability to suppress the production of IFN-γ from conventional T cells between CCR4-intact Tregs and CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 5D).
evidence: ELISA measurements comparing the suppressive effects of CCR4-intact and CCR4-deficient Tregs on IFN-γ production, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: The augmented Th1 cell responses in the peripheral lymphoid tissues of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice are partly due to impaired Treg-dependent regulation of dendritic cell function.
source: These results suggest that the augmented Th1 cell responses in the peripheral lymphoid tissues of Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice are partly due to impaired Treg-dependent regulation of DC function.
evidence: Inference based on coculture experiments showing impaired Treg suppression of DC activation and IFN-γ production.

claim: There is no difference in the migratory capacity of CCR4-intact or CCR4-deficient Kaede-expressing Tregs to the peripheral lymph nodes, spleen, or para-aortic lymph nodes of recipient Apoe-/- mice.
source: There was no difference in the migratory capacity of CCR4-intact or CCR4-deficient Kaede-expressing Tregs to the peripheral LNs, spleen, or para-aortic LNs of recipient Apoe-/- mice (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of transferred Kaede+ Tregs in lymphoid tissues, with reference to Figure 5F–H.

claim: There is a trend toward reduction in the proportion of CCR4-deficient Kaede-expressing Tregs in the aorta of recipient Apoe-/- mice.
source: Interestingly, we found a trend toward reduction in the proportion of CCR4-deficient Kaede-expressing Tregs in the aorta of recipient Apoe-/- mice (Figure 5I), suggesting that CCR4-deficient Tregs may have a reduced ability to migrate to the atherosclerotic aorta, but not to the peripheral lymphoid tissues, under hypercholesterolemia.
evidence: Flow cytometric analysis of transferred Kaede+ Tregs in aorta, with reference to Figure 5I.

claim: CCR4-deficient Tregs may have a reduced ability to migrate to the atherosclerotic aorta, but not to the peripheral lymphoid tissues, under hypercholesterolemia.
source: Interestingly, we found a trend toward reduction in the proportion of CCR4-deficient Kaede-expressing Tregs in the aorta of recipient Apoe-/- mice (Figure 5I), suggesting that CCR4-deficient Tregs may have a reduced ability to migrate to the atherosclerotic aorta, but not to the peripheral lymphoid tissues, under hypercholesterolemia.
evidence: Inference based on the trend toward reduced CCR4-deficient Treg accumulation in aorta but not in lymphoid tissues.

claim: CCR4 expression on Tregs plays a critical role in regulating Th1 cell responses in lymphoid tissues and may mediate Treg migration to the atherosclerotic aorta under hypercholesterolemia.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that CCR4 expression on Tregs plays a critical role in regulating Th1 cell responses in lymphoid tissues and may mediate Treg migration to the atherosclerotic aorta under hypercholesterolemia, which may cooperatively contribute to the reduction in early atherosclerosis by efficiently mitigating aortic inflammatory immune responses.
evidence: Summary inference based on multiple lines of data including suppression assays, DC coculture experiments, and Treg transfer experiments.

claim: There are no significant differences in the aortic sinus mean plaque area among Apoe-/- mice injected with saline, Apoe-/- Tregs, or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- Tregs.
source: Although there were no significant differences in the aortic sinus mean plaque area among the three groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), detailed analysis of the aortic root plaques at five different levels revealed significantly greater lesions in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-intact Tregs (Figure 6B), suggesting that the impaired CCR4-deficient Treg function is involved in the acceleration of atherosclerosis in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of mean atherosclerotic lesion area, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Detailed analysis of the aortic root plaques at five different levels reveals significantly greater lesions in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-intact Tregs.
source: Although there were no significant differences in the aortic sinus mean plaque area among the three groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), detailed analysis of the aortic root plaques at five different levels revealed significantly greater lesions in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-intact Tregs (Figure 6B), suggesting that the impaired CCR4-deficient Treg function is involved in the acceleration of atherosclerosis in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: Quantitative analysis of atherosclerotic lesion area at multiple levels, with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: The impaired CCR4-deficient Treg function is involved in the acceleration of atherosclerosis in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
source: Although there were no significant differences in the aortic sinus mean plaque area among the three groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), detailed analysis of the aortic root plaques at five different levels revealed significantly greater lesions in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice that were administered CCR4-intact Tregs (Figure 6B), suggesting that the impaired CCR4-deficient Treg function is involved in the acceleration of atherosclerosis in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: Inference based on Treg transfer experiments showing greater lesions with CCR4-deficient Tregs.

claim: There are no significant differences in body weight or plasma lipid profile among Apoe-/- mice injected with saline, Apoe-/- Tregs, or Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- Tregs.
source: There were no significant differences in body weight or plasma lipid profile among the three groups (Table 2).
evidence: Biochemical measurements showing no differences in body weight or lipid parameters, with reference to Table 2.

claim: The atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs show markedly reduced accumulation of macrophages compared to saline-injected Apoe-/- mice.
source: Compared with those of saline-injected Apoe-/- mice, the atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs showed markedly reduced accumulation of macrophages (Figure 6C) and CD4+ T cells (Figure 6D), whereas there were no differences in intraplaque accumulation of these inflammatory cells between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of macrophages in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: The atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs show markedly reduced accumulation of CD4+ T cells compared to saline-injected Apoe-/- mice.
source: Compared with those of saline-injected Apoe-/- mice, the atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs showed markedly reduced accumulation of macrophages (Figure 6C) and CD4+ T cells (Figure 6D), whereas there were no differences in intraplaque accumulation of these inflammatory cells between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of CD4+ T cells in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: There are no differences in intraplaque accumulation of macrophages and CD4+ T cells between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs.
source: Compared with those of saline-injected Apoe-/- mice, the atherosclerotic lesions of Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs showed markedly reduced accumulation of macrophages (Figure 6C) and CD4+ T cells (Figure 6D), whereas there were no differences in intraplaque accumulation of these inflammatory cells between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of inflammatory cells in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 6C and D.

claim: Macrophage accumulation in the aortic sinus atherosclerotic lesions is markedly higher in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs.
source: Notably, macrophage accumulation in the aortic sinus atherosclerotic lesions was markedly higher in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs than in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs (Figure 6C).
evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of macrophages comparing CCR4-intact and CCR4-deficient Treg transfer groups, with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Collagen content in atherosclerotic lesions is significantly higher in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs than in saline-injected Apoe-/- mice.
source: Collagen content in atherosclerotic lesions was significantly higher in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs than in saline-injected Apoe-/- mice, while no difference in collagen was observed between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 6E).
evidence: Histological quantification of collagen content in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: No difference in collagen content is observed between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs.
source: Collagen content in atherosclerotic lesions was significantly higher in Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-intact Tregs than in saline-injected Apoe-/- mice, while no difference in collagen was observed between saline-injected Apoe-/- mice and Apoe-/- mice injected with CCR4-deficient Tregs (Figure 6E).
evidence: Histological quantification of collagen content in atherosclerotic lesions, with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: CCR4 protects against early atherosclerosis partly by mediating Treg-dependent induction of a less inflammatory plaque phenotype.
source: Overall, we provide evidence that CCR4 protects against early atherosclerosis partly by mediating Treg-dependent induction of a less inflammatory plaque phenotype.
evidence: Summary inference based on Treg transfer experiments showing effects on plaque composition.

claim: Genetic deletion of CCR4 in hypercholesterolemic Apoe-/- mice accelerates the development of early atherosclerotic lesions in the aortic root that exhibit an inflammatory phenotype.
source: In the present study, we demonstrated that genetic deletion of CCR4 in hypercholesterolemic Apoe-/- mice accelerates the development of early atherosclerotic lesions in the aortic root that exhibit an inflammatory phenotype, associated with the augmentation of proatherogenic Th1 cell responses in the peripheral lymphoid tissues, para-aortic LNs, and atherosclerotic aorta.
evidence: Summary statement of main findings from the study.

claim: CCR4 expression on Tregs regulates the development of early atherosclerosis by suppressing Th1 cell responses in lymphoid tissues and possibly by mediating Treg migration to the atherosclerotic aorta.
source: Furthermore, T cell-DC coculture and Treg transfer experiments revealed that CCR4 expression on Tregs regulates the development of early atherosclerosis by suppressing Th1 cell responses in lymphoid tissues and possibly by mediating Treg migration to the atherosclerotic aorta.
evidence: Summary statement of mechanistic findings from coculture and transfer experiments.

claim: A novel role for the CCL17/CCL22–CCR4 axes in controlling early atherosclerosis via favorable modulation of the Th1 cell/Treg balance has been identified.
source: Thus, we identified a novel role for the CCL17/CCL22–CCR4 axes in controlling early atherosclerosis via favorable modulation of the Th1 cell/Treg balance.
evidence: Summary statement of the overall conclusion of the study.

claim: CD4+ or CD8+ T cells are the dominant populations in human and mouse atherosclerotic plaques.
source: Emerging experimental and clinical data obtained by single-cell RNA sequencing and mass cytometry have clearly shown that CD4+ or CD8+ T cells are the dominant populations in human (Fernandez et al., 2019) and mouse (Winkels et al., 2018) atherosclerotic plaques.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Fernandez et al., 2019; Winkels et al., 2018).

claim: Dysregulation of the balance of proatherogenic Th1 cells and anti-atherogenic Tregs has adverse effects on atherosclerotic disease.
source: Recent experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that dysregulation of the balance of proatherogenic Th1 cells and anti-atherogenic Tregs has adverse effects on atherosclerotic disease (Tanaka et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous literature (Tanaka et al., 2021).

claim: Th1 cells play a proatherogenic role.
source: Given the proatherogenic nature of Th1 cells (Gupta et al., 1997; Buono et al., 2005), our data indicate that augmented Th1 cell responses in peripheral lymphoid tissues, especially in atherosclerotic lesions, substantially contributed to atherosclerotic lesion formation in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Gupta et al., 1997; Buono et al., 2005).

claim: Th2 cells and some Th17 cells, but not Th1 cells, express CCR4.
source: As Th2 cells and some Th17 cells, but not Th1 cells, are known to express CCR4 (Griffith et al., 2014), the augmented Th1 cell responses observed in Ccr4-/-Apoe-/- mice do not seem to be direct effects of CCR4 deficiency and may involve other mechanisms.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous literature (Griffith et al., 2014).

claim: CCR4 plays a pivotal role in mediating Treg migration to inflammatory tissues.
source: In line with experimental studies in mouse models of inflammatory diseases showing a pivotal role for CCR4 in mediating Treg migration to inflammatory tissues (Yuan et al., 2007; Faustino et al., 2013), we found that CCR4 expression on Tregs may be critical for their migration to the atherosclerotic aorta, providing a possible mechanism for CCR4-dependent regulation of atherosclerosis.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Yuan et al., 2007; Faustino et al., 2013).

claim: The CCL22–CCR4 axis plays a crucial role in the contact of Tregs with dendritic cells and regulation of inflammatory responses.
source: T cell-DC coculture experiments clearly demonstrated that CCR4 expression on Tregs is critical for attenuating DC-dependent stimulation of Th1 cell responses by maintaining interactions between Tregs and DCs and Treg suppressive function, which is supported by the findings of a previous report showing a crucial role of the CCL22–CCR4 axis in the contact of Tregs with DCs and regulation of inflammatory responses (Rapp et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous literature (Rapp et al., 2019).

claim: T cell costimulatory signals such as the CD28–CD80/CD86 and CD27–CD70 pathways protect against atherosclerosis by systemically shifting the Th1 cell/Treg balance toward Treg responses.
source: T cell costimulatory signals such as the CD28–CD80/CD86 (Ait-Oufella et al., 2006) and CD27–CD70 (Winkels et al., 2017) pathways protect against atherosclerosis by systemically shifting the Th1 cell/Treg balance toward Treg responses.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Ait-Oufella et al., 2006; Winkels et al., 2017).

claim: Several approaches have been reported to mitigate atherosclerosis via modulation of the Th1 cell/Treg balance in the peripheral lymphoid tissues and atherosclerotic lesions of atherosclerosis-prone mice.
source: Several approaches involving treatment with cytokines (Dinh et al., 2012; Kasahara et al., 2014), antibodies (Sasaki et al., 2009; Kasahara et al., 2014; Steffens et al., 2006), an active form of vitamin D3 (Takeda et al., 2010), or ultraviolet B irradiation Sasaki et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2024 have been reported to mitigate atherosclerosis via modulation of the Th1 cell/Treg balance in the peripheral lymphoid tissues and atherosclerotic lesions of atherosclerosis-prone mice.
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations to previous literature (Dinh et al., 2012; Kasahara et al., 2014; Sasaki et al., 2009; Steffens et al., 2006; Takeda et al., 2010; Sasaki et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2024).

claim: The chemokine system plays an important role in the differentiation and migration of various subsets of T cells including Tregs and has been shown to be involved in the process of atherosclerosis.
source: The chemokine system plays an important role in the differentiation and migration of various subsets of T cells including Tregs and has been shown to be involved in the process of atherosclerosis (Noels et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous literature (Noels et al., 2019).

claim: Neither hematopoietic nor systemic CCR4 deficiency affected the development of advanced atherosclerotic lesions or Treg frequency in severely hypercholesterolemic mice.
source: However, previous studies showed that neither hematopoietic nor systemic CCR4 deficiency affected the development of advanced atherosclerotic lesions or Treg frequency in severely hypercholesterolemic mice (Weber et al., 2011; Döring et al., 2024).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Weber et al., 2011; Döring et al., 2024).

claim: The role of CCR4 may vary depending on the stages of atherosclerosis.
source: These findings suggest that the role of CCR4 may vary depending on the stages of atherosclerosis.
evidence: Inference based on the discrepancy between findings in early versus advanced atherosclerosis.

claim: Genetic deficiency of CCL17 ameliorated atherosclerotic lesion development by promoting Treg accumulation in lymphoid tissues and atherosclerotic lesions independently of the CCL17–CCR4 axis.
source: However, studies in hypercholesterolemic mice demonstrated that genetic deficiency of CCL17 ameliorated atherosclerotic lesion development by promoting Treg accumulation in lymphoid tissues and atherosclerotic lesions independently of the CCL17–CCR4 axis (Weber et al., 2011; Döring et al., 2024).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous literature (Weber et al., 2011; Döring et al., 2024).

claim: CCL17 restrains Treg homeostasis and accelerates atherosclerosis.
source: This suggests that CCL17 restrains Treg homeostasis and accelerates atherosclerosis, although the role of the CCL17–CCR4 axis in the regulation of Treg homeostasis and atherosclerosis remains elusive.
evidence: Inference based on findings from CCL17 deficiency studies.

claim: CCL17 deficiency increased Treg recruitment to the heart and attenuated myocardial inflammation and injury, which may be attributed to the cancellation of competitive inhibition of CCL22-mediated Treg chemotaxis by CCL17.
source: A study in mouse models of myocardial injury showed that CCL17 deficiency increased Treg recruitment to the heart and attenuated myocardial inflammation and injury, which may be attributed to the cancellation of competitive inhibition of CCL22-mediated Treg chemotaxis by CCL17 (Feng et al., 2022), suggesting that CCL17 may impair Treg homeostasis via the inhibition of the CCL22–CCR4 axis.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous literature (Feng et al., 2022).

claim: CCL17 may impair Treg homeostasis via the inhibition of the CCL22–CCR4 axis.
source: A study in mouse models of myocardial injury showed that CCL17 deficiency increased Treg recruitment to the heart and attenuated myocardial inflammation and injury, which may be attributed to the cancellation of competitive inhibition of CCL22-mediated Treg chemotaxis by CCL17 (Feng et al., 2022), suggesting that CCL17 may impair Treg homeostasis via the inhibition of the CCL22–CCR4 axis.
evidence: Inference based on findings from myocardial injury studies.

claim: The CCL22–CCR4 axis plays a dominant role in the prevention of atherosclerosis by promoting Treg function.
source: Given the crucial role of the CCL22–CCR4 axis in mediating the Treg suppressive function described above (Rapp et al., 2019), we propose that the CCL22–CCR4 axis plays a dominant role in the prevention of atherosclerosis by promoting Treg function, which may be inhibited by stimulating the CCL17–CCR4 axis.
evidence: Inference based on the role of CCL22–CCR4 in Treg function and the inhibitory effect of CCL17.

claim: CCR4 is an important negative regulator of atherosclerosis.
source: Our data suggest that CCR4 is an important negative regulator of atherosclerosis.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.
